chapterList.title: The Porter at the Gate
also: The Island That Was a Whale

s.t: A poor porter lived in Baghdad, and his name was Sinbad.
s.fr: Un pauvre porteur vivait à Bagdad, et son nom était Sinbad.

s.t: Each day he carried heavy loads in the hot streets.
s.fr: Chaque jour il portait de lourdes charges dans les rues chaudes.

s.t: One day he set his load down at the gate of a great house.
s.fr: Un jour il posa sa charge devant la porte d’une grande maison.

s.t: He heard a great feast inside.
s.fr: Il entendit une grande festin à l’intérieur.

paras.summary: A poor porter named Sinbad carries loads through the hot streets of Baghdad, and one day he sets his load down at the gate of a great house, where a feast is going on inside.

s.t: "The master of this house rests all day," the porter said.
s.fr: « Le maître de cette maison se repose toute la journée, » dit le porteur.

s.t: "I walk the hot streets under heavy loads, and my food is bread."
s.fr: « Je marche dans les rues chaudes sous de lourdes charges, et ma nourriture est du pain. »

s.t: "Why must one man walk all day, and one man rest and eat?"
s.fr: « Pourquoi un homme doit-il marcher toute la journée, et un autre se reposer et manger ? »

s.t: A servant heard him and went inside.
s.fr: Un serviteur l’entendit et entra à l’intérieur.

s.t: He came back and said, "My master asks for you."
s.fr: Il revint et dit, « Mon maître vous demande. »

paras.summary: The porter says aloud that the master rests all day while he walks under loads and eats bread; a servant hears him and comes back with word that the master asks for him.

s.t: The porter went in and stood in a great hall full of guests.
s.fr: Le porteur entra et se tint dans une grande salle pleine d’invités.

s.t: A rich man sat at the feast.
s.fr: Un homme riche était assis au festin.

s.t: "What is your name?" the man asked.
s.fr: « Quel est votre nom ? » demanda l’homme.

s.t: "I am Sinbad the porter," said the porter.
s.fr: « Je suis Sinbad le porteur, » dit le porteur.

s.t: "Sinbad is my name too, for I am Sinbad the Sailor," said the man.
s.fr: « Sinbad est mon nom aussi, car je suis Sinbad le Marin, » dit l’homme.

paras.summary: In the hall the porter meets a rich man at the feast, and when they trade names he learns that they share one — the master is Sinbad the Sailor.

s.t: "You think the sea gave me my gold and this great house."
s.fr: « Vous pensez que la mer m’a donné mon or et cette grande maison. »

s.t: "Seven times I went to sea, and seven times the sea nearly killed me."
s.fr: « Sept fois j’allai en mer, et sept fois la mer faillit me tuer. »

s.t: "Sit and eat, and hear the tales of my seven voyages."
s.fr: « Asseyez-vous, mangez, et écoutez les récits de mes sept voyages. »

s.t: The porter sat down, and Sinbad the Sailor began the first tale.
s.fr: Le porteur s’assit, et Sinbad le Marin commença le premier récit.

paras.summary: Sinbad the Sailor says the sea did not simply give him his gold, for it nearly killed him seven times, and he asks the porter to sit, eat, and hear the tales of his seven voyages.

s.t: The father of Sinbad the Sailor was a rich man of Baghdad.
s.fr: Le père de Sinbad le Marin était un homme riche de Bagdad.

s.t: He died and left young Sinbad his gold, his houses, and his land.
s.fr: Il mourut et laissa au jeune Sinbad son or, ses maisons, et sa terre.

s.t: Young Sinbad feasted with rich young men, and in one year the gold was gone.
s.fr: Le jeune Sinbad festoya avec de riches jeunes hommes, et en un an l’or disparut.

s.t: One morning he saw what was left, and he was afraid.
s.fr: Un matin il vit ce qui restait, et il fut effrayé.

s.t: He sold the houses and the land and gave the gold for goods to trade.
s.fr: Il vendit les maisons et la terre et donna l’or pour des marchandises à vendre.

paras.summary: Sinbad the Sailor's rich father dies and leaves him gold, houses, and land, but young Sinbad feasts with rich young men until the gold is gone; afraid of a poor man's life, he sells what is left and puts the gold into trade goods.

s.t: With his goods he went on a ship full of merchants.
s.fr: Avec ses marchandises il monta sur un navire plein de marchands.

s.t: The ship sailed for many days to far lands and far islands.
s.fr: Le navire navigua pendant de nombreux jours vers des terres lointaines et des îles lointaines.

s.t: At the far islands Sinbad sold his goods, and the trade made him rich.
s.fr: Aux îles lointaines Sinbad vendit ses marchandises, et le commerce le rendit riche.

s.t: One day the ship came to an island for water.
s.fr: Un jour le navire arriva à une île pour chercher de l’eau.

s.t: The men went ashore with food and a wooden tub, and made a fire on the sand.
s.fr: Les hommes débarquèrent avec de la nourriture et un baquet en bois, et allumèrent un feu sur le sable.

paras.summary: Sinbad boards a ship full of merchants, trades well at far islands, and grows rich, until one day the ship comes to an island for water and the men go ashore and make a fire on the sand.

s.t: But the island was not land at all.
s.fr: Mais l’île n’était pas de la terre du tout.

s.t: It was a great whale, and it had slept so long that sand and trees grew on its back.
s.fr: C’était une grande baleine, et elle avait dormi si longtemps que du sable et des arbres avaient poussé sur son dos.

s.t: The fire woke the whale, and the sand began to move under the men.
s.fr: Le feu réveilla la baleine, et le sable commença à bouger sous les hommes.

s.t: "To the ship!" said the captain.
s.fr: « Au navire ! » dit-il le capitaine.

s.t: The whale dived, and the island went down under the water.
s.fr: La baleine plongea, et l’île s’enfonça sous l’eau.

paras.summary: The island is really a great whale that has slept so long that sand and trees grew on its back; the fire wakes it, the sand moves, the captain calls the men to the ship, and the whale dives under the water.

s.t: The men went back to the ship, but the waves had carried Sinbad far from it.
s.fr: Les hommes retournèrent au navire, mais les vagues avaient emporté Sinbad loin de lui.

s.t: He took hold of the wooden tub, and the ship went on and left him.
s.fr: Il s’agrippa au baquet en bois, et le navire continua sa route et l’abandonna.

s.t: All night Sinbad held the tub.
s.fr: Toute la nuit, Sinbad tint le baquet.

s.t: In the morning the waves left him on the sand of a far island.
s.fr: Le matin, les vagues le laissèrent sur le sable d’une île lointaine.

paras.summary: The men get back to the ship, but the waves carry Sinbad too far; he takes hold of the wooden tub as the ship leaves him, and in the morning the waves leave him on the sand of a far island.

s.t: Men of the island king found Sinbad on the sand.
s.fr: Des hommes du roi de l’île trouvèrent Sinbad sur le sable.

s.t: The men gave him food and water and took him to the king.
s.fr: Les hommes lui donnèrent de la nourriture et de l’eau et le conduisirent vers le roi.

s.t: Sinbad told the king of the whale, the tub, and the lost ship.
s.fr: Sinbad parla au roi de la baleine, du baquet et du navire perdu.

s.t: The king was glad and gave Sinbad work at the harbor.
s.fr: Le roi fut content et donna à Sinbad du travail au port.

paras.summary: Men of the island king find Sinbad on the sand and take him to the king, who hears his tale and gives him work at the harbor.

s.t: Each day he saw the ships that came in from the sea.
s.fr: Chaque jour il voyait les navires qui entraient depuis la mer.

s.t: He wanted to go home to Baghdad.
s.fr: Il voulait rentrer chez lui à Bagdad.

s.t: One day a ship came in that Sinbad knew.
s.fr: Un jour un navire entra que Sinbad connaissait.

s.t: It was his own ship, the ship that had left him on the whale.
s.fr: C’était son propre navire, le navire qui l’avait laissé sur la baleine.

paras.summary: Sinbad watches the ships that come in and wants to go home to Baghdad, until one day his own ship comes in — the ship that left him on the whale.

s.t: "I am Sinbad," he said to the captain.
s.fr: « Je suis Sinbad, » dit-il au capitaine.

s.t: "Sinbad went down with the whale," said the captain.
s.fr: « Sinbad sombra avec la baleine, » dit le capitaine.

s.t: "Who are you?"
s.fr: « Qui êtes-vous ? »

s.t: "Open the bales in your ship, and I will say what is in each one."
s.fr: « Ouvrez les balles dans votre navire, et je dirai ce qui est dans chacune. »

s.t: Sinbad said what was in each bale before the men opened it.
s.fr: Sinbad dit ce qui était dans chaque balle avant que les hommes l’ouvrent.

s.t: At that the captain knew him, and he gave back all the goods.
s.fr: À cela le capitaine le reconnut, et il lui rendit tous les biens.

paras.summary: The captain does not know him at first, for he believes Sinbad went down with the whale, but Sinbad names what is in each bale before it is opened, and the captain gives back all his goods.

s.t: Sinbad sold his goods and was a rich man again.
s.fr: Sinbad vendit ses biens et fut de nouveau un homme riche.

s.t: Sinbad gave rich gifts to the king, and the king gave rich gifts to Sinbad.
s.fr: Sinbad offrit de riches cadeaux au roi, et le roi offrit de riches cadeaux à Sinbad.

s.t: He sailed home to Baghdad with more gold than he had lost.
s.fr: Il rentra chez lui à Bagdad avec plus d’or qu’il en avait perdu.

s.t: "That was the first voyage," said Sinbad the Sailor.
s.fr: « C’était le premier voyage, » dit Sinbad le Marin.

s.t: He gave the porter 100 pieces of gold and said, "Come again and hear more."
s.fr: Il donna au porteur 100 pièces d’or et dit : « Reviens et entends davantage. »

paras.summary: Sinbad sells his goods, trades rich gifts with the king, and sails home to Baghdad with more gold than he lost, where he makes his home in a great house; the tale ends, and Sinbad the Sailor gives the porter 100 pieces of gold and asks him to come again.

s.t: On the second night, the porter came back, and Sinbad the Sailor told of the second voyage.
s.fr: Le deuxième soir, le porteur revint, et Sinbad le Marin raconta le deuxième voyage.

s.t: For a year Sinbad rested in his great house, but in time he wanted the sea and far lands again.
s.fr: Pendant un an Sinbad se reposa dans sa grande maison, mais avec le temps il voulut de nouveau la mer et des terres lointaines.

s.t: He took goods and went to sea with a ship of merchants.
s.fr: Il prit des marchandises et alla en mer avec un navire de marchands.

s.t: One day the ship came to a green island.
s.fr: Un jour le navire arriva à une île verte.

s.t: Sinbad ate and slept under a tree.
s.fr: Sinbad mangea et dormit sous un arbre.

paras.summary: On the second night Sinbad the Sailor tells of the second voyage: after a year of rest he wanted the sea again, took goods, and sailed, until one day he ate and slept under a tree on a green island.

s.t: He woke, and the ship was gone.
s.fr: Il se réveilla, et le navire était parti.

s.t: No man had seen him under the tree, and the merchants had sailed on.
s.fr: Aucun homme ne l’avait vu sous l’arbre, et les marchands étaient partis.

s.t: Sinbad climbed a high tree and saw no ship on the sea.
s.fr: Sinbad grimpa dans un grand arbre et ne vit aucun navire sur la mer.

s.t: He saw a great white thing far over the trees.
s.fr: Il vit une grande chose blanche loin au-delà des arbres.

paras.summary: Sinbad wakes to find the ship gone, for no man saw him under the tree; he climbs a high tree, sees no ship, and sees instead a great white thing that he cannot name.

s.t: The sun went low, and a great bird came down over the island.
s.fr: Le soleil descendit bas, et un grand oiseau descendit sur l’île.

s.t: Its great wings made the island dark.
s.fr: Ses grandes ailes plongèrent l’île dans l’obscurité.

s.t: The bird sat down on the white thing, and Sinbad knew it was an egg.
s.fr: L’oiseau se posa sur la chose blanche, et Sinbad sut que c’était un œuf.

s.t: He knew the bird too, from tales the sailors told: it was a roc.
s.fr: Il connaissait aussi l’oiseau, grâce aux récits que les marins racontaient : c’était un roc.

s.t: The roc was a bird so great that it could take an elephant in its claws.
s.fr: Le roc était un oiseau si grand qu’il pouvait prendre un éléphant dans ses griffes.

paras.summary: At the end of the day a great bird comes down and makes the island dark with its wings, then sits on the white thing; Sinbad knows from sailors' tales that the thing is an egg and the bird is a roc, strong enough to take an elephant in its claws.

s.t: A roc could fly him from the island.
s.fr: Un roc pouvait le transporter hors de l’île.

s.t: In the dark, Sinbad tied himself with his turban to the leg of the bird and did not move.
s.fr: Dans l’obscurité, Sinbad s’attacha avec son turban à la patte de l’oiseau et ne bougea pas.

s.t: In the morning the roc flew high over far lands, with Sinbad on its leg.
s.fr: Le matin, le roc vola haut au-dessus de terres lointaines, avec Sinbad sur sa patte.

s.t: It came down in a great valley, and Sinbad made himself free of the leg.
s.fr: Il descendit dans une grande vallée, et Sinbad se libéra de la patte.

s.t: The roc took a great snake in its claws and flew over walls that no man could climb.
s.fr: Le roc prit un grand serpent dans ses griffes et vola par-dessus des murs qu’aucun homme ne pouvait escalader.

paras.summary: Hoping the roc can fly him from the island, Sinbad ties himself to its leg with his turban and holds still; in the morning the roc flies far, sets down in a great valley, and flies away with a snake, leaving Sinbad behind walls no man can climb.

s.t: The ground of the valley was all stones.
s.fr: Le sol de la vallée était tout couvert de pierres.

s.t: Sinbad took up a stone, and it was a diamond.
s.fr: Sinbad ramassa une pierre, et c’était un diamant.

s.t: The valley was full of diamonds, more than a man could hold.
s.fr: La vallée était pleine de diamants, plus qu’un homme n’en pouvait porter.

s.t: In Baghdad, one stone from this valley could make a poor man rich.
s.fr: À Bagdad, une pierre de cette vallée pouvait rendre un homme pauvre riche.

s.t: But a man could not eat diamonds, and Sinbad wanted bread and water more than stones.
s.fr: Mais un homme ne pouvait pas manger des diamants, et Sinbad voulait du pain et de l’eau plus que des pierres.

paras.summary: The valley floor is covered with diamonds, enough to make a poor man in Baghdad rich, but a man cannot eat diamonds, and Sinbad wants bread and water more than stones.

s.t: The walls of the valley had holes, and in the holes lived great snakes.
s.fr: Les murs de la vallée avaient des trous, et dans les trous vivaient de grands serpents.

s.t: Each snake was as long as a ship.
s.fr: Chaque serpent était aussi long qu’un navire.

s.t: By day the snakes hid in the holes, for fear of the great birds.
s.fr: Le jour, les serpents se cachaient dans les trous, par peur des grands oiseaux.

s.t: The sun went low, and the snakes came out of the holes.
s.fr: Le soleil descendit bas, et les serpents sortirent des trous.

paras.summary: Great snakes, each as long as a ship, live in holes in the valley walls; they hide by day for fear of the great birds and come out when the sun goes low.

s.t: Sinbad found a small hole with no snake in it.
s.fr: Sinbad trouva un petit trou où il n’y avait aucun serpent.

s.t: He went in and put stones all around him.
s.fr: Il entra et plaça des pierres tout autour de lui.

s.t: All night long the snakes went around and around the stones, and Sinbad did not sleep.
s.fr: Toute la nuit les serpents tournèrent et tournèrent autour des pierres, et Sinbad ne dormit pas.

s.t: In the morning the snakes went back into the holes.
s.fr: Le matin les serpents retournèrent dans les trous.

s.t: Sinbad came out from the stones.
s.fr: Sinbad sortit de derrière les pierres.

paras.summary: Sinbad finds an empty hole, puts stones all around himself, and sits without sleep while the snakes go around the stones all night, until morning sends them back into their holes.

s.t: A great piece of meat fell down on the stones.
s.fr: Un grand morceau de viande tomba sur les pierres.

s.t: Soon one more piece fell, and one more.
s.fr: Bientôt un autre morceau tomba, et un autre.

s.t: Sinbad saw men high on the walls of the valley, small and far.
s.fr: Sinbad vit des hommes haut sur les murs de la vallée, petits et loin.

s.t: He knew this valley from a tale merchants told in Baghdad.
s.fr: Il connaissait cette vallée grâce à un conte que des marchands avaient raconté à Bagdad.

s.t: The meat was a trick of the diamond merchants.
s.fr: La viande était un tour des marchands de diamants.

s.t: Sinbad sat down by the meat to wait.
s.fr: Sinbad s’assit près de la viande pour attendre.

paras.summary: Great pieces of meat begin to fall from above, and Sinbad sees men small and high on the walls; he knows this valley from a merchants' tale in Baghdad — the meat is a trick of the diamond merchants — and he sits down by the meat to wait.

s.t: No man could go down into the valley of diamonds and come out again.
s.fr: Aucun homme ne pouvait descendre dans la vallée des diamants et en ressortir.

s.t: The diamond merchants had a trick: they went up on the walls and threw down great pieces of raw meat.
s.fr: Les marchands de diamants avaient un truc : ils montaient sur les murs et jetaient de grands morceaux de viande crue.

s.t: The meat was soft and wet, and where it fell, diamonds stuck to it.
s.fr: La viande était molle et humide, et là où elle tombait, des diamants y adhéraient.

paras.summary: Sinbad remembers the tale merchants told in Baghdad: no man can go down into the valley of diamonds and come out, so the diamond merchants throw down great pieces of soft meat, and diamonds stick to the meat where it falls.

s.t: Great eagles had nests on the tops of the walls.
s.fr: De grands aigles avaient leurs nids au sommet des murs.

s.t: Each eagle came down for the meat and took it up to its nest.
s.fr: Chaque aigle descendait pour la viande et l’emportait jusqu’à son nid.

s.t: The diamonds went up with the meat.
s.fr: Les diamants montaient avec la viande.

s.t: At the nests the merchants shouted and threw stones, and the eagles flew away.
s.fr: Aux nids, les marchands criaient et jetaient des pierres, et les aigles s’envolaient.

s.t: The merchants took the diamonds out of the meat.
s.fr: Les marchands retiraient les diamants de la viande.

paras.summary: Great eagles nest on the tops of the walls and carry the meat up to their nests, and the merchants shout and throw stones until the eagles fly away, then take the diamonds out of the meat.

s.t: First Sinbad filled his coat with diamonds.
s.fr: D’abord, Sinbad remplit son manteau de diamants.

s.t: He tied himself with the turban under the greatest piece of meat.
s.fr: Il se lia avec le turban sous le plus grand morceau de viande.

s.t: A great eagle came down, took the meat in its claws, and flew up with meat and man.
s.fr: Un grand aigle descendit, prit la viande dans ses griffes, et s’envola avec la viande et l’homme.

s.t: It put them down in its nest, high on the wall.
s.fr: Il les déposa dans son nid, haut sur le mur.

s.t: A merchant ran to the nest, shouting and throwing stones, and the eagle flew away.
s.fr: Un marchand courut vers le nid, criant et lançant des pierres, et l’aigle s’envola.

s.t: Under the meat he found not diamonds but a man.
s.fr: Sous la viande il ne trouva pas des diamants mais un homme.

paras.summary: Sinbad fills his coat with diamonds and ties himself under the greatest piece of meat; an eagle carries meat and man up to its nest, and a merchant runs shouting to drive the eagle away.

s.t: The merchant fell back, afraid.
s.fr: Le marchand recula, effrayé.

s.t: "Do not fear me," said Sinbad, "for I have diamonds for you and for me."
s.fr: « Ne me craignez pas, » dit Sinbad, « car j’ai des diamants pour vous et pour moi. »

s.t: Sinbad filled the merchant's hands with diamonds, and the merchant was glad.
s.fr: Sinbad remplit les mains du marchand de diamants, et le marchand fut content.

s.t: The other merchants came, and Sinbad told his tale and gave diamonds to each one.
s.fr: Les autres marchands vinrent, et Sinbad raconta son histoire et donna des diamants à chacun.

s.t: He went home with the merchants over land, and came into Baghdad with his coat full of diamonds.
s.fr: Il rentra chez lui avec les marchands par voie de terre, et arriva à Bagdad avec son manteau plein de diamants.

paras.summary: The merchant finds a man under his meat and falls back afraid, but Sinbad calms him and fills his hands with diamonds; the other merchants hear his tale, each one is given diamonds, and Sinbad travels home over land to Baghdad with his coat full of diamonds.

s.t: "The sea will kill you," said Sinbad's friends.
s.fr: « La mer vous tuera, » dirent les amis de Sinbad.

s.t: But Sinbad sailed again.
s.fr: Mais Sinbad navigua de nouveau.

s.t: A great storm came over the sea, and it went on for a day and a night.
s.fr: Une grande tempête vint sur la mer, et elle dura un jour et une nuit.

s.t: It threw the ship onto the stones of an island, and the ship went to pieces.
s.fr: Il jeta le navire sur les rochers d’une île, et le navire se brisa en morceaux.

paras.summary: Friends tell Sinbad the sea will kill him, but he sails again; a great storm goes on for a day and a night, throws the ship onto the stones of an island, and the ship goes to pieces.

s.t: Sinbad and some of the men came out of the sea to the island.
s.fr: Sinbad et quelques-uns des hommes sortirent de la mer vers l’île.

s.t: On the island stood a great house of dark stone, with an open gate.
s.fr: Sur l’île se dressait une grande maison de pierre sombre, avec une porte ouverte.

s.t: The men went into the house and sat down.
s.fr: Les hommes entrèrent dans la maison et s’assirent.

s.t: At dark the ground shook, and the giant came to the house.
s.fr: À la nuit tombante, le sol trembla, et le géant vint à la maison.

s.t: He stood as high as 3 men, and his teeth were long.
s.fr: Il était aussi grand que 3 hommes, et ses dents étaient longues.

paras.summary: Sinbad and some of the men come out of the sea and find a great house of dark stone with an open gate; they go in to sit down, and at dark the ground shakes and the giant comes home, as high as 3 men, with long teeth.

s.t: The men hid in the dark of the house.
s.fr: Les hommes se cachèrent dans l’obscurité de la maison.

s.t: No man could fight him, for he was too strong.
s.fr: Aucun homme ne pouvait le combattre, car il était trop fort.

s.t: The giant took one of the men and ate him.
s.fr: Le géant prit un des hommes et le mangea.

s.t: The giant slept by the gate, and no man could go out.
s.fr: Le géant dormit près de la grille, et aucun homme ne pouvait sortir.

paras.summary: The men hide in the dark, for no man can fight one so strong; the giant takes one of the men and eats him, and all night the giant sleeps by the gate so that no man can go out.

s.t: In the morning the giant went away over the island.
s.fr: Le matin le géant s’en alla au-delà de l’île.

s.t: The men stood by the sea and wept.
s.fr: Les hommes se tinrent au bord de la mer et pleurèrent.

s.t: "We will leave this island, or we will die on it, man by man," said Sinbad.
s.fr: « Nous quitterons cette île, ou nous mourrons sur elle, homme par homme, » dit Sinbad.

paras.summary: In the morning the giant goes away over the island; the men weep by the sea, knowing he will come back at dark, and Sinbad says they will leave the island or die on it.

s.t: Some men said they would fight the giant in his sleep.
s.fr: Certains hommes dirent qu’ils combattraient le géant pendant son sommeil.

s.t: "A fight would wake him, and no man would live," said Sinbad.
s.fr: « Un combat le réveillerait, et aucun homme ne survivrait, » dit Sinbad.

s.t: "We will make rafts from the wood of the lost ship."
s.fr: « Nous ferons des radeaux avec le bois du navire perdu. »

s.t: The men made rafts from the wood, tied them with ropes, and hid them under trees.
s.fr: Les hommes fabriquèrent des radeaux avec le bois, les attachèrent avec des cordes, et les cachèrent sous des arbres.

paras.summary: Some men want to fight the giant in his sleep, but Sinbad says a fight would wake him and no man would live, so while the giant is away each day the men make rafts from the wood of the lost ship and hide them under trees.

s.t: At dark the men went back into the house, so the giant would not look for them.
s.fr: À la nuit tombante les hommes rentrèrent dans la maison, pour que le géant ne les cherche pas.

s.t: In the night the giant took one more man.
s.fr: Dans la nuit le géant prit un homme de plus.

s.t: On the third day the rafts were done, and the men pushed out on the water.
s.fr: Le troisième jour les radeaux étaient prêts, et les hommes s’élancèrent sur l’eau.

s.t: When the giant came home, he found no man in the house.
s.fr: Quand le géant rentra chez lui, il ne trouva pas d’homme dans la maison.

paras.summary: Each night the men go back into the house so the giant will not look for them, and one more man is taken; on the third day the rafts are done, and the men push out before the giant comes home to an empty house.

s.t: He went to the water and threw stones at the rafts.
s.fr: Il alla vers l’eau et lança des pierres sur les radeaux.

s.t: The stones went into the sea, and the rafts were too far out.
s.fr: Les pierres tombèrent dans la mer, et les radeaux étaient trop loin.

s.t: For 2 days and 2 nights the rafts were on the sea, and the food was gone.
s.fr: Pendant 2 jours et 2 nuits les radeaux furent sur la mer, et la nourriture était épuisée.

s.t: A trade ship found them at last and took the men on.
s.fr: Un navire marchand les trouva enfin et prit les hommes à bord.

s.t: The captain was a good man and gave them food and water.
s.fr: Le capitaine était un bon homme et leur donna de la nourriture et de l’eau.

paras.summary: The giant throws stones after the rafts, but they fall into the sea; after 2 days and 2 nights on the sea, a trade ship takes the men on, and its good captain gives them food and water.

s.t: The ship traded from port to port, and Sinbad did a sailor's work for his way home.
s.fr: Le navire commerçait de port en port, et Sinbad fit le travail d’un marin pour rentrer chez lui.

s.t: He came home to Baghdad with a purse of pearls the captain gave him for his work.
s.fr: Il rentra à Bagdad avec une bourse de perles que le capitaine lui donna pour son travail.

s.t: When the tale was done, the porter asked, "Why did you go back to the sea?"
s.fr: Quand le conte fut terminé, le porteur demanda, « Pourquoi êtes-vous retourné à la mer ? »

s.t: "At home I forgot the fear, but I did not forget the wonder," said Sinbad the Sailor.
s.fr: « À la maison j’oubliai la peur, mais je n’oubliai pas l’émerveillement, » dit-il, Sinbad le Marin.

paras.summary: Sinbad does a sailor's work from port to port for his way home and reaches Baghdad with a purse of pearls; when the porter asks why he went back to the sea, Sinbad says he forgot the fear but not the wonder.

s.t: On the fourth voyage the sea was calm for many days.
s.fr: Au cours du quatrième voyage, la mer fut calme pendant de nombreux jours.

s.t: In the dark of night the ship ran on stones and went down.
s.fr: Dans l’obscurité de la nuit, le navire heurta des pierres et coula.

s.t: The waves put Sinbad on a far shore, and he saw no other man in the water.
s.fr: Les vagues déposèrent Sinbad sur un rivage lointain, et il ne vit personne d’autre dans l’eau.

s.t: On the island were fruit trees and water.
s.fr: Sur l’île il y avait des arbres fruitiers et de l’eau.

paras.summary: The fourth voyage is calm until the ship runs onto stones in the dark and goes down; the waves carry Sinbad alone to a far shore, an island of fruit trees and water.

s.t: But when dark came, great snakes came out of holes in the ground.
s.fr: Mais quand la nuit tomba, de grands serpents sortirent de trous dans le sol.

s.t: That night Sinbad went high into a tree and did not sleep.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, Sinbad monta haut dans un arbre et ne dormit pas.

s.t: By day he made a wall of wood and sticks, too high for the snakes.
s.fr: Le jour, il construisit un mur de bois et de bâtons, trop haut pour les serpents.

s.t: He left one way in, and at dark he put wood over it.
s.fr: Il laissa une entrée, et à la nuit tombante il posa du bois dessus.

paras.summary: At dark great snakes come out of holes in the ground, and Sinbad spends the first night high in a tree; by day he makes a wall of wood and sticks too high for the snakes, with one way in that he shuts at dark.

s.t: All night the snakes went around and around the wall, but not one came in.
s.fr: Toute la nuit les serpents tournèrent en rond autour du mur, mais pas un n’entra.

s.t: When morning came, the snakes went into the ground, and Sinbad slept.
s.fr: Quand le matin arriva, les serpents rentrèrent dans le sol, et Sinbad dormit.

s.t: He lived so for many days, with fruit by day and the wall by night.
s.fr: Il vécut ainsi pendant de nombreux jours, avec des fruits le jour et le mur la nuit.

paras.summary: Night after night the snakes go around and around the wall but cannot come in, while Sinbad listens inside; he lives so for many days, and the wall of wood holds every night.

s.t: At last he saw a ship far out on the sea.
s.fr: Enfin il aperçut un navire au loin sur la mer.

s.t: He made a great fire on the shore and put green wood on it.
s.fr: Il fit un grand feu sur le rivage et posa du bois vert dessus.

s.t: The men on the ship saw the fire and came in for him.
s.fr: Les hommes sur le navire virent le feu et vinrent le chercher.

s.t: The captain heard his tale and gave him silk to trade on the way home.
s.fr: Le capitaine entendit son récit et lui donna de la soie à vendre sur le chemin du retour.

s.t: Sinbad came home from the fourth voyage with little gold, but with his life.
s.fr: Sinbad rentra chez lui après le quatrième voyage avec peu d’or, mais avec la vie sauve.

paras.summary: At last Sinbad sees a ship, makes a fire with green wood on the shore, and is taken on; the captain hears his tale and gives him silk to trade, and Sinbad comes home from the fourth voyage with little gold but with his life.

s.t: The fifth time, Sinbad took a ship of his own to sea, and other merchants came on it too.
s.fr: La cinquième fois, Sinbad prit un navire à lui pour aller en mer, et d’autres marchands montèrent à bord eux aussi.

s.t: At an island the men went ashore and came to a great egg.
s.fr: Sur une île, les hommes débarquèrent et arrivèrent devant un grand œuf.

s.t: Sinbad knew what it was, for he had seen the egg of a roc before.
s.fr: Sinbad savait ce que c’était, car il avait vu l’œuf d’un roc avant.

s.t: "Leave the egg," Sinbad said, "for the great birds will come back for it."
s.fr: « Laissez l’œuf, » dit Sinbad, « car les grands oiseaux reviendront le chercher. »

s.t: But the merchants would not hear him.
s.fr: Mais les marchands ne voulurent pas l’écouter.

paras.summary: On the fifth voyage Sinbad takes a ship of his own with other merchants; at an island the men find a great egg, and Sinbad, who knows the egg of a roc, tells them to leave it, but they will not hear him.

s.t: They broke the egg with stones and ate the young bird.
s.fr: Ils brisèrent l’œuf avec des pierres et mangèrent le jeune oiseau.

s.t: The day went dark, for the father and the mother had come back.
s.fr: Le jour s’assombrit, car le père et la mère étaient revenus.

s.t: The men took the ship out, but the birds came again, each one with a great stone in its claws.
s.fr: Les hommes sortirent le navire en mer, mais les oiseaux revinrent, chacun avec une grande pierre dans ses griffes.

s.t: One stone fell by the ship, and the sea went over it.
s.fr: Une pierre tomba près du navire, et la mer passa par-dessus.

s.t: The other stone fell on the ship and broke it in 2.
s.fr: L’autre pierre tomba sur le navire et le brisa en 2.

s.t: The other men went down with the ship and did not come up.
s.fr: Les autres hommes coulèrent avec le navire et ne remontèrent pas.

paras.summary: The merchants break the egg and eat the young bird; the father and the mother come back with great stones in their claws, one stone sends the sea over the ship, the other breaks the ship in 2, and the other men go down with it.

s.t: Sinbad took hold of a piece of the ship's wood.
s.fr: Sinbad saisit un morceau de bois du navire.

s.t: He came ashore on an island of fruit and streams, and ate the fruit.
s.fr: Il arriva sur une île de fruits et de ruisseaux, et mangea les fruits.

s.t: By a stream sat an old man with a white beard.
s.fr: Au bord d’un ruisseau était assis un vieux homme avec une barbe blanche.

s.t: With his hands he made signs at the stream, for he did not speak.
s.fr: Avec ses mains, il fit des signes vers le ruisseau, car il ne parlait pas.

s.t: Sinbad took the old man up on his shoulders and went into the stream.
s.fr: Sinbad prit le vieil homme sur ses épaules et entra dans le ruisseau.

paras.summary: Sinbad holds a piece of the ship's wood and comes ashore on an island of fruit and streams, where an old man sits by a stream and makes signs with his hands, for he does not speak; Sinbad takes him up on his shoulders and steps into the stream.

s.t: Over the stream, Sinbad went to set him down on the stones.
s.fr: De l’autre côté du ruisseau, Sinbad voulut le poser sur les pierres.

s.t: But the old man put his legs over Sinbad's shoulders and held on to his neck.
s.fr: Mais le vieil homme passa ses jambes sur les épaules de Sinbad et s’accrocha à son cou.

s.t: The legs were thin, but they were strong, and they would not let go.
s.fr: Les jambes étaient minces, mais elles étaient fortes, et elles ne lâchaient pas.

s.t: From that day, the old man sat on Sinbad's shoulders by day and by night, and would not come down.
s.fr: À partir de ce jour, le vieil homme resta sur les épaules de Sinbad le jour comme la nuit, et ne voulait pas descendre.

paras.summary: When Sinbad goes to set him down, the old man locks his thin, strong legs around Sinbad's neck and will not let go, and from that day he sits on Sinbad's shoulders by day and by night.

s.t: The old man made Sinbad walk under the fruit trees all day.
s.fr: L’vieux homme fit Sinbad marcher sous les arbres fruitiers toute la journée.

s.t: He ate the fruit from Sinbad's hands and gave him a little.
s.fr: Il mangea le fruit des mains de Sinbad et lui en donna un peu.

s.t: He was heavy, and Sinbad grew thin under him.
s.fr: Il était lourd, et Sinbad maigrit sous lui.

s.t: In sleep too, the old legs held Sinbad's neck.
s.fr: Dans le sommeil aussi, les vieilles jambes tenaient le cou de Sinbad.

paras.summary: The old man rides Sinbad under the fruit trees all day, eating from his hands and giving him little, and even in sleep the old legs hold Sinbad's neck.

s.t: Grapes grew all over that island.
s.fr: Des raisins poussaient partout sur cette île.

s.t: One day, under the trees, Sinbad took a dry gourd from the ground.
s.fr: Un jour, sous les arbres, Sinbad prit une gourde sèche par terre.

s.t: He put the juice of the grapes in the gourd.
s.fr: Il mit le jus des raisins dans la gourde.

s.t: He left it in the sun for some days, and the sun made the juice strong.
s.fr: Il la laissa au soleil pendant quelques jours, et le soleil rendit le jus fort.

s.t: The juice was wine, and Sinbad drank a little and sang.
s.fr: Le jus était du vin, et Sinbad en but un peu et chanta.

paras.summary: Grapes grow all over the island, so Sinbad puts their juice into a dry gourd and leaves it in the sun for some days, until the juice is strong wine; he drinks a little and sings as he walks.

s.t: The old man put out his hands for the gourd, and Sinbad gave it to him.
s.fr: Le vieux homme tendit ses mains vers la gourde, et Sinbad la lui donna.

s.t: The old man drank the wine down, and he drank it all.
s.fr: Le vieux homme but le vin jusqu’au bout, et il le but tout.

s.t: Soon the old man slept, and his legs let go.
s.fr: Bientôt le vieux homme s’endormit, et ses jambes lâchèrent prise.

s.t: Sinbad took him from his shoulders and set him down soft on the ground.
s.fr: Sinbad le prit de ses épaules et le posa doucement sur le sol.

paras.summary: The old man puts out his hands for the gourd and drinks all the wine; soon he sleeps, his legs let go, and Sinbad sets him down soft on the ground.

s.t: Sinbad walked, and Sinbad ran.
s.fr: Sinbad marcha, et Sinbad courut.

s.t: At the shore was a ship, and the men took Sinbad on.
s.fr: Au rivage se trouvait un navire, et les hommes prirent Sinbad à bord.

s.t: Sinbad told the men of the old man, and one old sailor knew the tale.
s.fr: Sinbad parla aux hommes du vieil homme, et un vieux marin connaissait le récit.

s.t: "That was the Old Man of the Sea," the old sailor said.
s.fr: « C’était le Vieux de la Mer, » dit le vieux marin.

s.t: "No man he took was free of him — you are the first."
s.fr: « Aucun homme qu’il prenait n’était libre de lui — vous êtes le premier. »

s.t: In every port Sinbad told his tale, and merchants gave him goods for the wonder of it.
s.fr: Dans chaque port Sinbad racontait son récit, et des marchands lui donnaient des marchandises pour l’émerveillement que cela suscitait.

s.t: He came home to Baghdad with a full purse.
s.fr: Il rentra chez lui à Bagdad avec une bourse pleine.

paras.summary: Sinbad runs to the shore, where the men of a ship take him on; an old sailor tells him he is the first man to get free of the Old Man of the Sea, and in every port Sinbad's tale brings him goods, so he comes home to Baghdad with a full purse.

s.t: Merchants came to Sinbad and asked him to go on a sixth voyage with them.
s.fr: Des marchands vinrent voir Sinbad et lui demandèrent de partir en un sixième voyage avec eux.

s.t: Far out on that voyage, the captain lost the way.
s.fr: Loin dans ce voyage, le capitaine perdit la route.

s.t: A great wind took the ship into seas no man on it knew.
s.fr: Un grand vent poussa le navire dans des mers qu’aucun homme à bord ne connaissait.

s.t: One morning the captain threw down his turban and wept.
s.fr: Un matin, le capitaine jeta son turban à terre et pleura.

paras.summary: Merchants ask Sinbad to lead a sixth voyage, but far out the captain loses the way, a great wind takes the ship into unknown seas, and one morning the captain throws down his turban and weeps.

s.t: "A current takes the ship," he said.
s.fr: « Un courant emporte le navire, » dit-il.

s.t: "It runs to a black mountain, and no ship comes back from it."
s.fr: « Il court vers une montagne noire, et aucun navire n’en revient. »

s.t: The fast current took the ship on the stones under the mountain and broke it.
s.fr: Le courant rapide emporta le navire sur les pierres sous la montagne et le brisa.

s.t: No man but Sinbad came out of the sea alive.
s.fr: Aucun homme sauf Sinbad ne sortit vivant de la mer.

paras.summary: The captain says a current takes the ship and runs to a black mountain from which no ship comes back; the current breaks the ship on the stones under the mountain, and only Sinbad comes out of the sea alive.

s.t: The shore was full of the goods and the wood of lost ships.
s.fr: Le rivage était plein de marchandises et de bois de navires perdus.

s.t: The cliffs went up and up, and no man could climb them.
s.fr: Les falaises montaient toujours plus haut, et aucun homme ne pouvait les escalader.

s.t: On that shore was a river, and every river Sinbad knew ran into the sea.
s.fr: Sur ce rivage se trouvait une rivière, et chaque rivière que Sinbad connaissait coulait vers la mer.

s.t: This river ran from the sea into the land, to a great cave deep under the mountain.
s.fr: Cette rivière coulait de la mer vers la terre, jusqu’à une grande grotte profonde sous la montagne.

paras.summary: The shore is covered with the goods and wood of ships lost over many years, the cliffs cannot be climbed, and strangest of all, a river runs from the sea into the land, to a great cave deep under the mountain.

s.t: In the lost ships was food for some days.
s.fr: Dans les navires perdus se trouvait de la nourriture pour quelques jours.

s.t: Sinbad was afraid of the dark way, but more afraid of the empty shore.
s.fr: Sinbad avait peur de la voie sombre, mais il avait encore plus peur du rivage vide.

s.t: He would go with the river.
s.fr: Il suivrait la rivière.

s.t: He made a raft from the wood of the wrecks and tied it with ropes.
s.fr: Il construisit un radeau avec le bois des épaves et l’attacha avec des cordes.

s.t: On the raft he put silk and jewels from the lost ships.
s.fr: Sur le radeau il posa de la soie et des joyaux des navires perdus.

s.t: He took the raft into the river and went in under the mountain.
s.fr: Il mena le radeau dans la rivière et entra sous la montagne.

s.t: The day grew small at his back, and was gone.
s.fr: Le jour diminua derrière lui, et disparut.

paras.summary: Sinbad eats what food the lost ships hold, and, more afraid of the empty shore than of the dark way, he builds a raft from the wood of the wrecks, puts silk and jewels on it, and rides the river in under the mountain until the day behind him is gone.

s.t: Under the mountain the dark was deep, and Sinbad could not see his hands.
s.fr: Sous la montagne l’obscurité était profonde, et Sinbad ne pouvait pas voir ses mains.

s.t: The stone of the mountain came low over him, and he made himself small on the raft.
s.fr: La pierre de la montagne descendait bas au-dessus de lui, et il se fit petit sur le radeau.

s.t: The river ran on and on in the dark, and at last Sinbad slept.
s.fr: La rivière coulait sans fin dans l’obscurité, et enfin Sinbad s’endormit.

s.t: He woke in the light of day, on a slow river in a land of green fields.
s.fr: Il se réveilla dans la lumière du jour, sur une rivière lente dans un pays de champs verts.

paras.summary: Under the mountain the dark is so deep that Sinbad cannot see his hands; the stone comes down low over the raft, the river runs on and on, and at last he sleeps and wakes in daylight on a slow river among green fields.

s.t: They gave him food and brought him to the king.
s.fr: Ils lui donnèrent de la nourriture et le conduisirent au roi.

s.t: The land was Serendib, and the king of Serendib was good to strangers.
s.fr: Le pays était Serendib, et le roi de Serendib était bon envers les étrangers.

s.t: The king knew Sinbad's name, for merchants brought his tales over the sea.
s.fr: Le roi connaissait le nom de Sinbad, car des marchands apportaient ses récits par-delà la mer.

paras.summary: The people of the fields wonder at him, feed him, and take him to the king of Serendib, who is good to strangers and already knows Sinbad's name from the tales merchants have carried over the sea.

s.t: Sinbad told the king all his tales, from the whale to the river under the mountain.
s.fr: Sinbad raconta au roi toutes ses récits, depuis la baleine jusqu’à la rivière sous la montagne.

s.t: Of all the tales, the king asked for the valley of diamonds 2 times.
s.fr: De toutes les récits, le roi demanda la vallée des diamants 2 fois.

s.t: In time Sinbad wanted to go home, and the king gave him great gifts.
s.fr: Avec le temps, Sinbad voulut rentrer chez lui, et le roi lui donna de grands cadeaux.

s.t: One gift was a cup made from one red stone, and with it went spice and silk.
s.fr: Un cadeau était une coupe faite d’une pierre rouge, et avec elle partaient des épices et de la soie.

s.t: The king sent him home on a ship of Serendib, with the gifts and the goods of the raft.
s.fr: Le roi le renvoya chez lui sur un navire de Serendib, avec les cadeaux et les marchandises du radeau.

paras.summary: Sinbad tells the king all his tales, and the king asks for the valley of diamonds 2 times; when Sinbad wants to go home, the king gives him great gifts, among them a cup made from one red stone, and sends him home on a ship of Serendib.

s.t: Sinbad came home from the sixth voyage with more than from all the voyages before it.
s.fr: Sinbad rentra chez lui du sixième voyage avec plus que de tous les voyages avant lui.

s.t: "6 voyages," said the porter, and he counted on his fingers.
s.fr: « 6 voyages, » dit-il le porteur, et il compta sur ses doigts.

s.t: "One voyage more," said Sinbad.
s.fr: « Un voyage de plus, » dit Sinbad.

s.t: The porter went home, and came back for the last tale.
s.fr: Le porteur rentra chez lui, et revint pour la dernière histoire.

paras.summary: Sinbad comes home from the sixth voyage with more than from all the voyages before it; the porter counts 6 voyages on his fingers, Sinbad promises one voyage more, and the porter comes back for the last tale.

s.t: "I am done with the sea," Sinbad said when he came home the sixth time.
s.fr: « J’en ai fini avec la mer, » dit Sinbad quand il rentra chez lui la sixième fois.

s.t: But the king of Baghdad sent for Sinbad and said, "Take my gifts to the king of Serendib."
s.fr: Mais le roi de Bagdad envoya chercher Sinbad et dit, « Porte mes cadeaux au roi de Serendib. »

s.t: No man says no to a king.
s.fr: Nul homme ne dit non à un roi.

s.t: Sinbad went to sea one more time and gave the gifts to the king of Serendib.
s.fr: Sinbad repartit en mer une fois de plus et offrit les cadeaux au roi de Serendib.

paras.summary: Sinbad says he is done with the sea, but the king of Baghdad sends him one more time with gifts for the king of Serendib, and no man says no to a king.

s.t: On the way home, pirates took the ship.
s.fr: Sur le chemin du retour, des pirates prirent le navire.

s.t: They sold the men in a port, and a rich master bought Sinbad.
s.fr: Ils vendirent les hommes dans un port, et un riche maître acheta Sinbad.

s.t: "Can you shoot with a bow?" said the master, and Sinbad said he could.
s.fr: « Sais-tu tirer à l’arc ? » dit-il le maître, et Sinbad dit qu’il le pouvait.

s.t: The master gave him a bow and arrows and brought him to a great tree by a road.
s.fr: Le maître lui donna un arc et des flèches et l’amena à un grand arbre au bord d’une route.

s.t: "Shoot the elephants of the road, and bring me the great teeth."
s.fr: « Tire sur les éléphants de la route, et apporte-moi les grandes dents. »

s.t: "For the teeth are ivory, and ivory makes men rich."
s.fr: « Car les dents sont de l’ivoire, et l’ivoire rend les hommes riches. »

paras.summary: On the way home pirates take the ship and sell the men; a rich master buys Sinbad, gives him a bow and arrows, and sets him in a great tree to shoot the elephants of the road, for their teeth are ivory, and ivory makes men rich.

s.t: Sinbad waited in the tree with the bow.
s.fr: Sinbad attendit dans l’arbre avec l’arc.

s.t: The elephants came down the road slow, the young ones by the old.
s.fr: Les éléphants descendirent la route lentement, les jeunes à côté des vieux.

s.t: Sinbad put the arrow to the bow, and he put the bow down.
s.fr: Sinbad mit la flèche à l’arc, et il posa l’arc.

s.t: He did not want to kill the great beasts.
s.fr: Il ne voulait pas tuer les grandes bêtes.

s.t: Day after day, Sinbad brought the master no teeth.
s.fr: Jour après jour, Sinbad n’apporta aucune dent au maître.

paras.summary: Sinbad waits in the tree, but when the elephants come down the road with their young, he puts the arrow to the bow and puts the bow down, for he does not want to kill the great beasts, and day after day he brings the master no teeth.

s.t: "Shoot," said the master, "or you will go back to the port."
s.fr: « Tire, » dit-il, le maître, « ou tu retourneras au port. »

s.t: In the morning, all the elephants of the road came around his tree.
s.fr: Le matin, tous les éléphants de la route vinrent autour de son arbre.

s.t: The greatest elephant put its trunk around Sinbad and lifted him from the tree.
s.fr: Le plus grand éléphant enroula sa trompe autour de Sinbad et le souleva de l’arbre.

s.t: It set him on its back and took him into the hills.
s.fr: Il le posa sur son dos et l’emmena dans les collines.

paras.summary: The master says Sinbad will go back to the port if he does not shoot; but in the morning the elephants come all around the tree, and the greatest elephant lifts Sinbad down with its trunk, sets him on its back, and carries him into the hills.

s.t: The elephant went into the green hills with Sinbad on its back.
s.fr: L’éléphant entra dans les collines vertes avec Sinbad sur son dos.

s.t: It came to an open ground in the hills and put Sinbad down.
s.fr: Il arriva à un terrain ouvert dans les collines et déposa Sinbad.

s.t: All that ground was white with the teeth and the bones of elephants dead many years.
s.fr: Tout ce terrain était blanc de dents et d’os d’éléphants morts depuis de nombreuses années.

s.t: A man could not count the teeth of that ground in a day.
s.fr: Un homme ne pouvait pas compter les dents de ce terrain en un jour.

paras.summary: The elephant carries Sinbad into the green hills to an open ground, white with the teeth and bones of elephants dead many years, more than a man could count, and the ground is quiet.

s.t: Old elephants came to this ground to die, year after year, and no man knew it.
s.fr: Les vieux éléphants venaient mourir sur ce terrain, année après année, et aucun homme ne le savait.

s.t: This was the graveyard of the elephants.
s.fr: C’était le cimetière des éléphants.

s.t: The men could take the teeth of the dead, and never kill elephants.
s.fr: Les hommes pouvaient prendre les dents des morts, et ne jamais tuer les éléphants.

paras.summary: Old elephants come to this ground to die, year after year — it is the graveyard of the elephants — and Sinbad sees why he was brought: men can take the teeth of the dead and never kill an elephant for them.

s.t: The elephant took Sinbad back down the hills to the tree again.
s.fr: L’éléphant ramena Sinbad de nouveau en bas des collines jusqu’à l’arbre.

s.t: Sinbad put his hand on its trunk, and the elephant went slow into the trees.
s.fr: Sinbad posa sa main sur sa trompe, et l’éléphant avança lentement dans les arbres.

s.t: Sinbad told the master all that he had seen in the hills.
s.fr: Sinbad raconta au maître tout ce qu’il avait vu dans les collines.

s.t: The master went with him into the hills, and it was all true.
s.fr: Le maître y alla avec lui, et c’était tout vrai.

paras.summary: The elephant carries Sinbad back to the tree, Sinbad lays his hand on its trunk, and it goes slow away into the trees; he tells the master all, and when the master goes to see, it is all true.

s.t: "You have made me a rich man," said the master.
s.fr: « Vous m’avez rendu riche, » dit-il le maître.

s.t: "From this day you are a free man."
s.fr: « À partir d’aujourd’hui, vous êtes un homme libre. »

s.t: For a month his men went into the hills and carried heavy ivory down to the master's house.
s.fr: Pendant un mois, ses hommes allèrent dans les collines et portèrent de lourds ivoires jusqu’à la maison du maître.

s.t: The master gave Sinbad ivory of his own and put him on a ship for home.
s.fr: Le maître donna à Sinbad de l’ivoire qui lui appartenait et le mit sur un navire pour rentrer chez lui.

s.t: Sinbad came home to Baghdad from the seventh and last voyage a rich man.
s.fr: Sinbad rentra chez lui à Bagdad après le septième et dernier voyage, homme riche.

s.t: He gave gold to the poor of Baghdad and rested in his great house.
s.fr: Il donna de l’or aux pauvres de Bagdad et se reposa dans sa grande maison.

s.t: Sinbad never went to sea again.
s.fr: Sinbad ne retourna jamais en mer.

paras.summary: The master calls himself a rich man, sets Sinbad free, and after a month of carrying ivory gives Sinbad ivory of his own and a ship for home; Sinbad comes home from the seventh and last voyage rich, gives gold to the poor of Baghdad, and never goes to sea again.

s.t: When the last tale was done, the hall was quiet.
s.fr: Quand le dernier conte fut terminé, la salle était silencieuse.

s.t: For a long time the porter said nothing.
s.fr: Pendant longtemps le porteur ne dit rien.

s.t: "Seven times you went to sea," the porter said at last.
s.fr: « Sept fois vous allâtes en mer, » dit le porteur à la fin.

s.t: "Seven times the sea nearly killed you, and seven times you came home."
s.fr: « Sept fois la mer vous tua presque, et sept fois vous rentrâtes chez vous. »

s.t: "No man in the world tells seven such tales of the sea."
s.fr: « Aucun homme dans le monde ne raconte sept telles récits de la mer. »

paras.summary: When the last tale is done the hall is quiet, and the porter, who has not spoken, says at last that Sinbad went to sea seven times, nearly died seven times, and came home seven times — no man in the world tells seven such tales.

s.t: "At your gate I put my load down and said that the master of the house rests all day."
s.fr: « À votre porte j’ai posé ma charge et dit que le maître de la maison se repose toute la journée. »

s.t: "I know what work bought that rest."
s.fr: « Je sais quel travail a acheté ce repos. »

s.t: "Your gold did not come to you by luck."
s.fr: « Votre or ne vint pas à vous par chance. »

s.t: At that, Sinbad the Sailor laughed, and the guests laughed with him.
s.fr: À cela, Sinbad le Marin rit, et les invités rirent avec lui.

s.t: "No, my friend," he said.
s.fr: « Non, mon ami, » dit-il.

s.t: "It came by work, as your bread comes to you."
s.fr: « Il vint par le travail, comme votre pain vient à vous. »

paras.summary: The porter recalls what he said at the gate about the master who rests all day, and says he knows now what work bought that rest, for the gold did not come by luck; Sinbad laughs and agrees — it came by work, as the porter's bread comes.

s.t: He put a purse of 100 gold pieces in the porter's hands.
s.fr: Il mit une bourse de 100 pièces d’or dans les mains du porteur.

s.t: It was the seventh purse of gold that came home with the porter.
s.fr: C’était la septième bourse d’or qui revint chez le porteur.

s.t: "Come and eat at my table when you will," said Sinbad the Sailor.
s.fr: « Venez manger à ma table quand vous voudrez, » dit-il Sinbad le Marin.

s.t: The porter came again, and again, and always ate at that table with him.
s.fr: Le porteur revint encore, et encore, et mangea toujours à cette table avec lui.

paras.summary: Sinbad puts a seventh purse of 100 gold pieces into the porter's hands, the guests smile at the porter's thanks, and Sinbad asks him to eat at his table when he will, which the porter does again and again.

s.t: Porter and sailor had one name between them, and in the end one table.
s.fr: Le porteur et le marin avaient un nom commun entre eux, et à la fin une seule table.

s.t: When men in the streets said gold came by luck, the porter told them of the seven voyages.
s.fr: Quand des hommes dans les rues disaient que l’or venait par chance, le porteur leur parlait des sept voyages.

paras.summary: Porter and sailor share one name and, in the end, one table; the two Sinbads grow old as friends, the porter never eats dry bread again, and when men in the streets say gold comes by luck, he tells them of the seven voyages.
